rebalance_callable_by_any_caller.meaning: rebalanceFunds() can be invoked by an arbitrary caller because it has no access control modifier

reentrancy_guard_absent.meaning: rebalanceFunds() lacks a nonReentrant modifier guarding its external custodian transfer

custodian_is_contract.meaning: the custodian address is a contract able to re-enter during the external transfer

token_callback_enabled.meaning: the vault token is an ERC777 or callback-enabled token that can invoke a callback during transfer

excess_drained_twice.meaning: excess is drained twice from the vault via reentrancy during the external custodian transfer

assumptions: rebalanceFunds() performs an external _vaultToken.transfer(custodian, excess) call as described in rc_external_call_no_guard.
The malicious custodian re-enters rebalanceFunds() during the external transfer, as described in a_reenter_transfer.

unresolved.description: Report does not quantify the excess amount or the number of reentrant transfers beyond the qualitative 'drain excess twice'; the drain-twice relation is encoded as a grounded Boolean.

limitations: Drain-twice is conditional on the custodian being a contract and the token being ERC777/callback-enabled; these are potential, not observed, conditions.
No concrete vault balance or excess magnitude is given, so the effect is represented qualitatively rather than numerically.
Other impacts (event spam, DoS delay, temporary under-collateralization) are not formalized by this plan.
